regulations_extracts.reg_2_05:
2.05  Conditions applicable to visas
(1)For subsection 41(1) of the Act, a visa is subject to any conditions specified for that Subclass of visa in Schedule 2, subject to subregulation (2) and regulation 2.25AE.
Note:Regulation 2.40A prescribes conditions in relation to special purpose visas taken to have been granted to airline positioning crew members and airline crew members.
(2)For subsection 41(3) of the Act, the conditions that the Minister is permitted to impose on a visa are the conditions (if any) specified as permitted for that Subclass of visa in Schedule 2.
Note:Conditions referred to by number in Schedule 2 are set out in Schedule 8: see the definition of condition in regulation 1.03.
(3)For the purposes of subsections 29(2) and (3) of the Act (which deal with the period during which the holder of a visa may travel to, enter and remain in Australia), the limits on the period within which a person may:
(a)remain in Australia; or
(b)travel to, enter, and remain in Australia;
as the case requires, under the authority of a visa of a particular subclass are specified in the relevant Part of Schedule 2.
(4)For subsection 41(2A) of the Act, the circumstances in which the Minister may waive a condition of a kind described in paragraph 41(2)(a) of the Act are that:
(a)since the person was granted the visa that was subject to the condition, compelling and compassionate circumstances have developed:
(i)over which the person had no control; and
(ii)that resulted in a major change to the person’s circumstances; and
(b)if the Minister has previously refused to waive the condition, the Minister is satisfied that the circumstances mentioned in paragraph (a) are substantially different from those considered previously; and
(c)if the person asks the Minister to waive the condition, the request is in writing.
(4AA)For subsection 41(2A) of the Act, a further circumstance in which the Minister may waive condition 8503 in relation to a visa is that the holder of the visa has a genuine intention to apply for:
(a)a General Skilled Migration visa; or
(c)a Subclass 186 (Employer Nomination Scheme) visa; or
(d)a Subclass 187 (Regional Sponsored Migration Scheme) visa; or
(e)a Subclass 188 (Business Innovation and Investment (Provisional)) visa; or
(ea)a Subclass 191 (Permanent Residence (Skilled Regional)) visa; or
(f)a Subclass 482 (Skills in Demand) visa; or
(g)a Subclass 494 (Skilled Employer Sponsored Regional (Provisional)) visa.
(4AB)For subsection 41(2A) of the Act, further circumstances in which the Minister may waive condition 8503 in relation to a visa are that the holder of the visa:
(a)either:
(i)holds a safe haven enterprise visa; or
(ii)is a lawful noncitizen who has ever held a safe haven enterprise visa; and
(b)satisfies the requirements of subregulation 2.06AAB(2).
(4AC)For paragraph 41(2B)(b) of the Act, the following visas are prescribed:
(a)a Subclass 400 (Temporary Work (Short Stay Specialist)) visa;
(b)a Subclass 457 (Temporary Work (Skilled)) visa;
(ba)a Subclass 482 (Skills in Demand) visa;
(c)a Subclass 482 (Temporary Skill Shortage) visa;
(d)a Subclass 988 (Maritime Crew) visa held by a petroleum export tanker crew member.
(5A)For subsection 41(2A) of the Act, further circumstances in which the Minister may waive condition 8534 in relation to a visa are that the holder of the visa:
(a)has completed the course for which the visa was granted; and
(b)has a genuine intention to apply for:
(i)a General Skilled Migration visa; or
(iii)a Subclass 186 (Employer Nomination Scheme) visa; or
(iv)a Subclass 187 (Regional Sponsored Migration Scheme) visa; or
(v)a Subclass 188 (Business Innovation and Investment (Provisional)) visa; or
(va)a Subclass 191 (Permanent Residence (Skilled Regional)) visa; or
(vi)a Subclass 482 (Skills in Demand) visa; or
(vii)a Subclass 494 (Skilled Employer Sponsored Regional (Provisional)) visa.

conditions.title_ko: 근로 전면 금지 (No Work)
conditions.title_en: No Work in Australia
conditions.summary_ko: 호주 체류 중 보수 지급 여부와 무관하게 호주에서 통상 대가가 지급되는 형태의 일(근로)을 일체 할 수 없습니다.
conditions.summary_en: You must not engage in any work in Australia, defined under reg 1.03 as activity that normally attracts remuneration.
forbidden_ko: 유급 취업, 아르바이트, 캐주얼·파트타임 근로 일체 금지
호주 내 사업체 운영 또는 ABN 기반 프리랜서·용역 활동 금지
통상 급여가 지급되는 직무를 '무급 체험·수습' 명목으로 대신 수행하는 행위 금지
forbidden_en: Any paid employment, casual shifts, or part-time work in Australia
Operating an Australian business or working on an ABN/contractor basis
Performing unpaid trials or duties that would normally attract wages
obligations_ko: 체류 기간 내내 무근로 상태 유지 (관광·방문·치료·비근로 브리징 목적 준수)
obligations_en: Refrain from work throughout your stay in Australia
exceptions_ko: 순수 무급 자원봉사(유급 인력을 대체하지 않는 자선·비영리 봉사) 및 순수 관광·가사
방문자(600) 등의 제한적 예외: 호주 외 대학 학점 연계 무급 실습·단순 참관(직접 작업 불가) 등 사전 허가 시
브리징 비자(010/030/050 등) 소지자가 심각한 재정적 곤궁(financial hardship)을 입증해 근로 제한 해제 신청 가능
exceptions_en: Genuine unpaid volunteering that does not displace a paid worker
Limited visitor permissions (e.g. observation without working or overseas-course unpaid placement with approval)
Bridging visa holders (010/030/050) may apply for a new bridging visa without 8101 by proving compelling need to work (financial hardship)
conditions.waiver_ko: 원칙적 웨이버 대상은 아니며, 브리징 비자 소지자는 재정적 곤궁(Compelling Need to Work) 증빙으로 근로 허용 브리징 비자 재신청이 가능합니다.
conditions.waiver_en: Not waived via reg 2.05(4); eligible bridging visa holders may apply for work rights on compelling-need (financial hardship) grounds.

clause_notes_ko.text: 단 1문장('must not engage in work in Australia')이지만, reg 1.03의 'work' 정의('호주에서 통상 보수가 따르는 활동') 때문에 돈을 받지 않아도 일반 직원이 할 일을 대신 하면 위반이 될 수 있습니다.

clause_notes_en.text: Although only one sentence, 'work' under reg 1.03 means an activity that normally attracts remuneration in Australia—so unpaid labour in a commercial role can still breach 8101.

scenarios.q_ko: 한국 회사 원격 재택근무나 한국 계좌로 급여를 받는 일도 위반인가요?
scenarios.q_en: Is remote work for an overseas employer paid into an overseas bank allowed?
scenarios.a_ko: 단순 이메일 확인이나 짧은 업무 연락을 넘어 호주 체류 중 실질적 근로를 제공하면 호주 내 'work'에 해당할 위험이 있습니다(특히 장기 체류·정규 근무 형태). 구체적 업무 형태와 기간에 따른 개별 검토가 필요합니다.
scenarios.a_en: While brief incidental contact (e.g., checking emails) is distinct from ongoing work, performing regular substantive duties while physically in Australia can risk breaching 8101 regardless of where the bank account is located.

scenarios.q_en: Can I do unpaid volunteer work?
scenarios.a_ko: 영리 목적 사업체의 인건비를 대체하지 않고 순수하게 비영리·자선 목적으로 참여하는 자원봉사만 허용됩니다. 카페·농장 등에서 '숙식 제공(WWOOF)'이나 '무급 트라이얼'로 일하는 것은 통상 유급 근로에 해당해 위험합니다.
scenarios.a_en: Only genuine non-profit volunteering that would not otherwise be paid work is permitted. Unpaid commercial trials or work-for-accommodation arrangements typically risk breaching 8101.

conditions.statutory_text: 8101The holder must not engage in work in Australia.
statutory_paragraphs: 8101The holder must not engage in work in Australia.
conditions.dha_web_title: 8101 - No work
conditions.dha_web_summary:
You must not work in Australia.
This means when in Australia, you must not do
work that a person would normally get paid for.
conditions.dha_web_scenario:
For visitor visa holders only
With our permission, you can only:
do unpaid work relating and credited to your study if you are studying in a university outside Australia
see how people work in an industry, as long as you are not doing the work yourself
To seek permission, submit a letter about your situation with your visa application and supporting documentation.
If your situation changes after you arrive in Australia and you need to work you will need to apply for a new Visitor visa (Tourist stream) requesting permission to work.
You will need to prove:
you have financial hardship because of your new situation
you or your family member is likely to need the government's help
you have compelling personal reasons to work in Australia such as a serious accident or illness
for reasons that you cannot change, you or your immediate family cannot return home
you have no choice but to work in Australia
Decisions are made on a case-by-case situation at the discretion of the processing office or Minister.
If you are not being paid you can, without our permission:
do
volunteer work
do incidental work online for your job in your home country
do short-term domestic or care-giving work for a family member

conditions.title_ko: 학업·연수 직접 관련 근로 외 금지
conditions.title_en: Work Only Related to Course of Study or Training
conditions.summary_ko: 승인된 학업이나 연수(트레이닝) 과정에 직접 연결된 근로만 허용되며, 일반 아르바이트나 별도 취업은 금지됩니다.
conditions.summary_en: You may only engage in work directly related to your approved course of study or training; unrelated jobs are prohibited.
forbidden_ko: 연수·학업 프로그램과 무관한 일반 파트타임·아르바이트 근무
승인 기관 외 타 사업장에서의 별도 소득 활동
forbidden_en: Any paid or unpaid work unrelated to your nominated study or training program
obligations_ko: 모든 근로 활동이 등록된 연수·학업 커리큘럼 범위 내에 있는지 유지
obligations_en: Keep all work strictly within the scope of your approved study or training
exceptions_ko: 교육·연수 과정 자체에 포함된 실습·훈련(work-based training)은 허용
exceptions_en: Work that forms part of your approved course of study or training
conditions.waiver_ko: 웨이버 규정이 없으며, 다른 직무로 일하려면 해당 근무가 가능한 별도 비자를 신청해야 합니다.
conditions.waiver_en: Cannot be waived; unrelated work requires a visa permitting that employment.

clause_notes_ko.text: 훈련비자(예: 구 402/442/현행 407 일부 승계 등) 계열에서 연수 커리큘럼 외 아르바이트를 막기 위한 조항입니다.

clause_notes_en.text: Restricts employment strictly to work directly tied to the holder's study or training course.

conditions.statutory_text: 8102The holder must not engage in work in Australia (other than in relation to the holder’s course of study or training).
statutory_paragraphs: 8102The holder must not engage in work in Australia (other than in relation to the holder’s course of study or training).
conditions.dha_web_title: 8102 - Not work other than in relation to study or training
conditions.dha_web_summary:
You can only work if it is related to your course of study or training.
Understanding your work rights
The Department is working with the Fair Work Ombudsman to help employees and employers understand and follow Australian Workplace laws.
Information on pay rates, shift calculations, leave arrangements and notice and redundancy entitlements is in the
Pay and Conditions Tool (PACT).
The Fair Work Ombudsman website has more information on workplace rights and entitlements for
visa holders and migrant workers.
For the full list of conditions relevant to your visa, see the Federal Register of Legislation.
conditions.dha_web_scenario:
You can do
volunteer work that is not related to your course of study or training if:
it is not interfering with your course of study or training
is of benefit to the community
it would not otherwise be undertaken in return for wages by an Australian resident, and
it is genuinely voluntary
You can take up a tutoring or research assistant role if:
it relates to the field of the occupational training programme
it is beneficial to the training you are undertaking, and
the role is with your sponsoring university

conditions.title_ko: 장관 사전 서면 허가 없는 근로 금지 (870 등)
conditions.title_en: No Work Without Minister's Written Permission
conditions.summary_ko: 이민성 장관의 서면 허가를 받기 전까지는 호주에서 어떠한 근로도 할 수 없으며, 주로 단기 부모초청(870) 등에 부과됩니다.
conditions.summary_en: You must not undertake work in Australia without prior written permission from the Minister (commonly imposed on Subclass 870).
forbidden_ko: 이민성의 사전 서면 근로 허가 없이 호주 내 유·무급 취업 및 사업 활동 금지
forbidden_en: Working in Australia without prior written ministerial permission
obligations_ko: 서면 허가를 받은 경우에도 허가서에 명시된 특정 직무((a))와 허가 기간((b)) 범위 내에서만 근무
obligations_en: If permission is granted, comply strictly with any specified work type (a) and duration (b)
exceptions_ko: 장관(또는 위임 심사관)이 특정 업무 또는 기간을 지정해 서면 허가한 경우에만 예외적으로 허용
exceptions_en: Work expressly authorised in writing by the Minister for specified work or a specified period
conditions.waiver_ko: 8101과 달리 조항 자체에 '서면 허가 신청' 구조가 내장돼 있으나, 870 임시부모비자 등에서는 원칙적으로 근로를 허용하지 않습니다.
conditions.waiver_en: Permission must be sought in writing; rarely granted outside exceptional visa contexts.

clause_notes_ko.text: 장관의 서면 허가는 특정 업무((a))만 허용하거나 특정 기간((b))으로 한정해 부여될 수 있습니다.

clause_notes_en.text: Written permission may be restricted to specified work (a) or a specified time period (b).

exceptions_ko: (3) 주신청자가 석사(Master) 또는 박사(Doctoral) 학위 과정인 경우(coursework 석사 포함) 동반가족은 주신청자 개강 후 시간 제한 없이 근로 가능
(2A)/(2B)/(2C) 신청 당시 본인 또는 주신청자가 근로 가능한 실질·브리징 비자를 소지했다면 개강 전에도(Subclass 500 기준 2주 48시간까지) 근로 가능
exceptions_en: (3) If the primary student's course is for a Masters (including coursework Masters) or Doctoral degree, family members have unlimited work rights once permitted to work
(2A)–(2C) If either the holder or primary applicant held a visa with work rights at lodgement, the dependant may work up to 48 hrs/fortnight (for Subclass 500) even before the course starts
conditions.waiver_ko: 웨이버 규정이 없으므로 학사/디플로마 동반가족이 48시간 초과 근로를 하려면 별도 취업 비자를 취득해야 합니다.
conditions.waiver_en: Not waivable; exceeding the cap breaches the visa condition and risks s 116 cancellation.

clause_notes_ko.text: 법 조문 (1)항의 문구 '40시간'을 (3A)항이 Subclass 500 및 연계 브리징 비자에 한해 '48시간'으로 대체 적용합니다.
원래 주신청자 개강 전엔 일할 수 없으나((2)), 신청 당시 본인((2A))이나 주신청자((2B))가 일할 수 있는 비자를 갖고 있었다면 개강 전부터 (3A) 기준인 2주 48시간까지 일할 수 있습니다.
주신청자가 석사(Masters) 또는 박사(Doctoral) 과정이면 동반가족은 48시간 제한을 받지 않습니다(주신청자 본인 8105와 달리 '연구 석사'로 한정하지 않고 석사 전반 포함).
'fortnight'는 급여 지급일이 아니라 반드시 월요일(Monday)에 시작하는 연속 14일을 뜻합니다.

clause_notes_en.text: Subclause (1) retains '40 hours' as base drafting, while (3A) substitutes '48 hours' for Subclass 500 and associated bridging visas.
Bars work until the primary student starts their course unless (2A) or (2B) applied at visa lodgement—in which case up to 48 hours/fortnight (under 3A) applies immediately.
Removes the fortnightly hour cap for family members of Masters or Doctoral students (unlike 8105, not restricted to Masters by Research).
A fortnight is strictly any 14-day period beginning on a Monday—not an employer's pay cycle.

conditions.drift_ko: 이민성 웹 안내문(see-your-visa-conditions) 첫 줄에는 구 기준인 '40 hours a fortnight'가, 바로 아래 불릿에는 현행 '48 hours a fortnight'가 동시에 적혀 있어 혼선을 줍니다. 법령 8104(3A)에 따라 Subclass 500(및 연계 브리징 비자)에는 48시간이 적용됩니다.
conditions.drift_en: Home Affairs' web page contradicts itself by stating '40 hours a fortnight' in paragraph 1 and '48 hours' below. Under Schedule 8 cl 8104(3A), Subclass 500 and related bridging visas use 48 hours.

scenarios.q_ko: 방학 기간에는 주신청자처럼 동반가족(학사 과정 배우자)도 무제한으로 일할 수 있나요?
scenarios.q_en: Can a Bachelor student's spouse work unlimited hours during semester breaks?
scenarios.a_ko: 아닙니다. 주신청자(8105)와 달리 동반가족의 8104 조항에는 '방학 중(course not in session) 면제' 조항이 없습니다. 학사·VET 과정 학생의 동반가족은 방학 중에도 2주 48시간 상한을 지켜야 합니다.
scenarios.a_en: No. Unlike Condition 8105 for primary students, Condition 8104 has no 'out-of-session' exemption—dependants of Bachelor/VET students remain capped at 48 hours per fortnight even during holidays.

scenarios.q_ko: 주신청자가 석사(Coursework)를 공부하면 배우자도 무제한 근무가 가능한가요?
scenarios.q_en: If the primary student studies a Coursework Masters, can the spouse work unlimited hours?
scenarios.a_ko: 네, 주신청자 개강 후에는 가능합니다. 8105(주신청자)는 '연구 석사(by research)'만 무제한인 반면, 8104(3)은 석사(masters degree) 전반과 박사(doctoral degree) 과정 동반가족의 시간 제한을 면제합니다.
scenarios.a_en: Yes, once permitted to work (after course commencement unless (2A)/(2B) applies). Clause 8104(3) covers all Masters degrees and Doctorates, unlike 8105(2)(b) which limits Masters exemptions to research degrees.

conditions.statutory_text:
8104(1)The holder must not engage in work for more than 40 hours a fortnight while the holder is in Australia.
(2)Subject to subclauses (2A) and (2B), if the holder is a member of the family unit of a person who satisfies the primary criteria for the grant of a student visa, the holder must not engage in work in Australia until the person who satisfies the primary criteria has commenced a course of study.
(2A)Subclause (2) does not apply to the holder if:
(a)at the time of applying for the visa, the holder held a substantive visa or a bridging visa (the previous visa); and
(b)the holder was permitted to work in Australia during the period that the previous visa was in effect.
(2B)Subclause (2) does not apply to the holder if the person who satisfies the primary criteria for the grant of the student visa:
(a)held a substantive visa or a bridging visa (the previous visa) at the time of applying for the student visa; and
(b)was permitted to work in Australia during the period that the previous visa was in effect.
(2C)If subclause (2) does not apply to the holder because of subclause (2A) or (2B), then despite subclause (1), the holder may engage in work for more than 40 hours a fortnight:
(a)while the holder is in Australia; and
(b)before the course of study mentioned in subclause (2) commences.
(3)If the course of study mentioned in subclause (2) is for the award of a masters or doctoral degree, then despite subclause (1), the holder may engage in work for more than 40 hours a fortnight while the holder is in Australia.
(3A)If the visa held is a Subclass 500 (Student) visa, or a bridging visa granted on the basis of a valid application for a Subclass 500 (Student) visa, this clause applies as if the reference in subclauses (1), (2C) and (3) to 40 hours were instead a reference to 48 hours.
(4)In this clause:
fortnight means the period of 14 days commencing on a Monday.

conditions.dha_web_title: 8104 - Work limitation
conditions.dha_web_summary:
This condition means you cannot work more than 40 hours a fortnight, unless you are a family member of a Student visa holder.
Family members of a Student visa holder
Family members of a Student visa holder cannot work before the student’s course starts. That is unless the Student visa holder or their family member held another visa that allowed them to work in Australia.
Working while the course is in session:
Family members can work up to 48 hours a fortnight while the course is in session.
If the student is studying a Master’s Degree by Research or Doctoral Degree, they and their family members can work more than 48 hours a fortnight.
If the student is studying a Master’s Degree by Coursework, or a Master’s Degree (Extended), their family members can also work more than 48 hours a fortnight. However, the student can still only work up to 48 hours a fortnight while their course is in session.
A fortnight is a period of 14 days starting on a Monday.
Working when the course is not in session:
Student visa holders can work unlimited hours when their course is not in session.
Their family members still have limited work rights.
Make sure to check your visa conditions regularly, including your work rights.
To check your visa details, go to
VEVO.
Employers seeking to hire the family member of a primary Student visa holder should get evidence of the following:
the relationship, such as a visa grant letter, marriage or birth certificate
that the primary Student visa holder has commenced their course, such as a Confirmation of Enrolment or a letter from the relevant education provider.
Employers who have hired a family member with this visa condition should ensure they are not working more hours than the employee’s visa allows.
Understanding your work rights
The department is working with the Fair Work Ombudsman to help employees and employers understand and follow Australian Workplace laws.
Information on pay rates, shift calculations, leave arrangements and notice and redundancy entitlements is in the Pay and Conditions Tool (PACT).
For more information on workplace rights and entitlements for visa holders and migrant workers visit
The Fair Work Ombudsman
For the full list of conditions relevant to your visa, see the Federal Register of Legislation.

conditions.summary_ko: 학생비자(500) 주신청자는 코스 시작 전엔 일할 수 없고(이전 비자 근로권 보유 예외), 학기 중에는 2주 48시간을 넘겨 일할 수 없습니다.

수업 진행 기간(in session, 시험기간 포함) 중 2주 48시간 초과 근무

Working more than 48 hours in any Monday-starting fortnight while your course is in session (including exam periods)

obligations_en: Check every consecutive 2-week (Monday-to-Sunday) window so no overlapping pair exceeds 48 hours
exceptions_ko: (2)(a) CRICOS 등록상 학업의 필수 요건으로 명시된 의무 실습 근로
(2)(b) 연구 중심 석사(Masters by Research) 또는 박사(Doctoral) 과정 개강 후 근로 무제한

exceptions_en: (2)(a) Mandatory work placement registered in CRICOS as a course requirement
(2)(b) Unlimited hours once a Masters by Research or Doctoral degree has commenced
Unlimited hours during scheduled course breaks when your course is not in session
conditions.waiver_ko: 웨이버 규정이 없으며, 학기 중 1~2시간만 넘겨도 s 116(1)(b) 비자 취소 사유가 됩니다.
conditions.waiver_en: No waiver available; even minor over-hours breaches create s 116 cancellation exposure.

clause_notes_ko.text: 워킹홀리데이 등 근로 가능 비자를 소지한 채 호주에서 500을 신청했다면 (1B)에 따라 새 코스 시작 전에도 근로가 가능합니다(단, 8105(1) 학기 제한은 개강 시 적용).
(1)항 원문 '40시간'을 (2A)항이 Subclass 500 및 연계 브리징 비자에 한해 '48시간'으로 대체 적용합니다.
CRICOS 등록 필수 실습((a))과 연구석사·박사 과정 개강 후((b))는 48시간 상한을 적용받지 않습니다.
2주(fortnight)는 반드시 월요일에 시작하는 14일입니다. 예: 1주차 10시간 + 2주차 38시간 + 3주차 20시간 일하면 2~3주차 합산이 58시간이 되어 위반입니다.

clause_notes_en.text: If you held a substantive or bridging visa permitting work when lodging your Subclass 500 application, (1B) lifts the pre-commencement work ban.
Subclause (2A) substitutes '48 hours' for the base '40 hours' wording in (1) for Subclass 500 and related bridging visas.
Exempts CRICOS-mandatory work components (a) and commenced Masters by Research / Doctoral degrees (b).
A fortnight starts every Monday; you must check rolling pairs (Week 1+2 AND Week 2+3) so neither exceeds 48 hours.

scenarios.q_en: If I work 10h in Week 1, 38h in Week 2, and 18h in Week 3, is that a breach?
scenarios.a_ko: 네, 위반입니다. 1~2주차 합은 48시간이지만, 2~3주차 합이 56시간(38+18)이 되어 2주 단위(매주 월요일 기산 14일) 48시간 상한을 넘습니다.
scenarios.a_en: Yes, that breaches 8105. Weeks 1+2 equal 48 hours, but Weeks 2+3 equal 56 hours (38+18), exceeding 48 hours in that Monday-starting fortnight.

scenarios.q_ko: Coursework 석사 과정 학생도 무제한으로 일할 수 있나요?
scenarios.q_en: Can a Coursework Masters student work unlimited hours?
scenarios.a_ko: 아닙니다. 8105(2)(b) 예외는 'Masters degree by research(연구 석사)'와 박사(Doctoral) 과정만 해당합니다. 일반 수업 석사(Coursework) 주신청자는 학기 중 2주 48시간 제한을 받습니다.
scenarios.a_en: No. Only a Masters by Research or Doctoral degree qualifies under 8105(2)(b); Coursework Masters students remain capped at 48 hours/fortnight in session.

conditions.dha_web_title: 8105 - Work limitation
conditions.dha_web_summary:
This condition means you cannot work in Australia before your course starts unless at the time of applying for this visa, you held another visa that permitted you to work in Australia.
You also cannot work more than 48 hours a fortnight when your course of study or training is in session.
A course of study is in session:
for the duration of the school semesters (including when exams are being held)
you take another course that will count towards your main course during a term break.
If you can work over 48 hours a fortnight
You can only work over 48 hours a fortnight if:
you hold a Student visa granted in relation to a masters degree by research or doctorate degree and your masters degree by research or doctorate degree has started​​
it is a registered part of your course that is mandatory, that was specified as a requirement of the course when the course particulars were entered into the Commonwealth Register of Institutions and Courses for Overseas Students
A course is not in session:
during scheduled course breaks
if your course was deferred or suspended in line with
Standard 9 of the National Code of Practice for Providers of Education and Training to Overseas Students​ ​
if you hold a valid visa and have completed your course as listed on your confirmation of enrolment
if your enrolment has been cancelled due to the default of your education provider and until you get a new enrolment and start the course.
A fortnight is a period of 14 days starting on a Monday.
An example of a Student visas holder’s 48 hours a fortnight working limit is:
week 1: 15 hours work
week 2: 30 hours work
week 3: 30 hours work
week 4: 10 hours work.
The student may not have breached their work conditions in the fortnight comprising the 14 days of weeks 1 and 2 (45 hours worked) or in the fortnight comprising the 14 days of weeks 3 and 4 (40 hours). However, if in session the student will be in breach of their work conditions, in the fortnight comprising the 14 days of weeks 2 and 3 (60 hours worked).
For example: a student is studying a commercial cookery course on a subclass 500 visa and is offered work experience during school holidays. The Student works 75 hours a fortnight and is allowed to work unlimited hours while the course is not in session. The Student visa holder did not break their work condition.
Work experience is included in a student’s work restriction of 48 hours a fortnight whether it is paid or unpaid.
The exception to this is if a work experience unit forms a mandatory component of a student’s course and is included in the CRICOS registration of that course. In this circumstance, the work experience will not be included in the student’s work restriction of 48 hours a fortnight. Any work experience/work placement that is not a mandatory course requirement, or that is in excess of the period required in the course registration, is included in a student’s work limitation of 48 hours a fortnight.
For example: a pharmacy student undertaking a mandatory 4 week block of on the job training has unlimited work rights for the purpose and duration of the work placement, as documented in the registered course structure.
Examples of definition of work:
You do a shift at a restaurant as part of a roster, but not during your rostered unpaid meal break.
You are a taxi driver who has signed in and is ready to receive passengers, until you sign out for a break or your shift ends.
As a Student visa holder, you are considered to have worked if you have:
attended a place of work for a period by a roster or timesheet (but not during unpaid breaks)
been ‘clocked on’ to an electronic system that records work activity
received remuneration for work, as indicated in a payslip you have been given (unless you give documentary evidence that you were not working during this time).
You can work more than one job as long as the total hours are not more than 48 hours in a fortnight.
If you are an employer seeking to hire a Student visa holder, you should request evidence that they commenced their course. This evidence can be a confirmation of enrolment or a letter from the education provider.
Employers who have hired a Student visa holder should ensure that the student/employee is not working more hours than the employee’s visa allows.
Understanding your work rights
The Department is working with the Fair Work Ombudsman to help employees and employers understand and follow Australian Workplace laws.
Information on pay rates, shift calculations, leave arrangements and notice and redundancy entitlements is in the Pay and Conditions Tool (PACT).
The Fair Work Ombudsman website has more information on workplace rights and entitlements for
visa holders and migrant workers.
For the full list of conditions relevant to your visa, see the
Federal Register of Legislation.​

conditions.statutory_text:
8107(1)If the visa is not a visa mentioned in subclause (3) or (4), and was granted to enable the holder to be employed in Australia, the holder must not:
(a)cease to be employed by the employer in relation to which the visa was granted; or
(b)work in a position or occupation inconsistent with the position or occupation in relation to which the visa was granted; or
(c)engage in work for another person or on the holder’s own account while undertaking the employment in relation to which the visa was granted.
(2)If the visa is not a visa mentioned in subclause (3) or (4), and subclause (1) does not apply, the holder must not:
(a)cease to undertake the activity in relation to which the visa was granted; or
(b)engage in an activity inconsistent with the activity in relation to which the visa was granted; or
(c)engage in work for another person or on the holder’s own account inconsistent with the activity in relation to which the visa was granted.
(3)If the visa is, or the last substantive visa held by the applicant was, a Subclass 457 (Temporary Work (Skilled)) visa that was granted on the basis that the holder met the requirements of subclause 457.223(2) or (4) (as in force before 18 March 2018):
(a)the holder:
(i)must work only in the occupation listed in the most recently approved nomination for the holder; and
(ii)unless the circumstances in subclause (3A) apply:
(A)must work only for the party to a labour agreement or former party to a labour agreement who nominated the holder in the most recently approved nomination; or
(B)if the sponsor is, or was, a standard business sponsor who was lawfully operating a business in Australia at the time of the sponsor’s approval as a standard business sponsor, or at the time of the last approval of a variation to the sponsor’s term of approval as a standard business sponsor—must work only in a position in the business of the sponsor or an associated entity of the sponsor; or
(C)if the sponsor is or was a standard business sponsor who was not lawfully operating a business in Australia, and was lawfully operating a business outside Australia, at the time of the sponsor’s approval as a standard business sponsor, or at the time of the last approval of a variation to the sponsor’s term of approval as a standard business sponsor—must work only in a position in the business of the sponsor; and
(aa)subject to paragraph (c), the holder must:
(i)if the holder was outside Australia when the visa was granted—commence work within 90 days after the holder’s arrival in Australia; and
(ii)if the holder was in Australia when the visa was granted—commence work within 90 days after the holder’s visa was granted; and
(b)the holder may cease to work in accordance with paragraph (a) for a period, but:
(i)any such period must not exceed 180 consecutive days; and
(ii)the total number of days on which the holder does not work in accordance with paragraph (a) must not exceed 365 during the visa period for the holder’s visa; and
(c)if the holder is required to hold a licence, registration or membership that is mandatory to perform the occupation nominated in relation to the holder, in the location where the holder’s position is situated—the holder:
(i)must hold the licence, registration or membership while the holder is performing the occupation; and
(ii)if the holder was outside Australia when the visa was granted—the holder must hold that licence, registration or membership within 90 days after the holder’s arrival in Australia; and
(iii)if the holder was in Australia when the visa was granted—the holder must hold that licence, registration or membership within 90 days after the holder’s visa was granted; and
(iv)must notify the Department, in writing as soon as practicable if an application for the licence, registration or membership is refused; and
(v)must comply with each condition or requirement to which the licence, registration or membership is subject; and
(vi)must not engage in work that is inconsistent with the licence, registration or membership, including any conditions or requirements to which the licence, registration or membership is subject; and
(vii)must notify the Department, in writing as soon as practicable if the licence, registration or membership ceases to be in force or is revoked or cancelled.
(3A)For subparagraph (3)(a)(ii), the circumstances are that:
(a)the holder’s occupation is specified in an instrument in writing for subparagraph 2.72(10)(e)(ii) or (iii) as in force before 18 March 2018; or
(b)the holder is continuing to work for the sponsor, or the associated entity of the sponsor, for the purpose of fulfilling a requirement under a law relating to industrial relations and relating to the giving of notice.
(4)If the visa is:
(a)a Subclass 401 (Temporary Work (Long Stay Activity)) visa; or
(b)a Subclass 402 (Training and Research) visa; or
(ba)a Subclass 420 (Temporary Work (Entertainment)) visa;
the holder must not:
(c)cease to engage in the most recently nominated occupation, program or activity in relation to which the holder is identified; or
(d)engage in work or an activity that is inconsistent with the most recently nominated occupation, program or activity in relation to which the holder is identified; or
(e)engage in work or an activity for an employer other than the employer identified in accordance with paragraph 2.72A(7)(a) as in force before 19 November 2016 (subject to subregulation 2.72A(8) as in force before that day) in the most recent nomination in which the holder is identified.
(5)If the visa is a subclass 407 (Training) visa, the holder must not:
(a)cease to engage in the most recently nominated program in relation to which the holder is identified; or
(b)engage in work or an activity that is inconsistent with the most recently nominated program in relation to which the holder is identified; or
(c)engage in work or an activity for an employer other than an employer identified in accordance with paragraph 2.72A(8)(a) (subject to subregulation 2.72A(9)) in the most recent nomination in which the holder is identified.
statutory_paragraphs: 8107(1)If the visa is not a visa mentioned in subclause (3) or (4), and was granted to enable the holder to be employed in Australia, the holder must not:
(a)cease to be employed by the employer in relation to which the visa was granted; or
(b)work in a position or occupation inconsistent with the position or occupation in relation to which the visa was granted; or
(c)engage in work for another person or on the holder’s own account while undertaking the employment in relation to which the visa was granted.
(2)If the visa is not a visa mentioned in subclause (3) or (4), and subclause (1) does not apply, the holder must not:
(a)cease to undertake the activity in relation to which the visa was granted; or
(b)engage in an activity inconsistent with the activity in relation to which the visa was granted; or
(c)engage in work for another person or on the holder’s own account inconsistent with the activity in relation to which the visa was granted.

(3)If the visa is, or the last substantive visa held by the applicant was, a Subclass 457 (Temporary Work (Skilled)) visa that was granted on the basis that the holder met the requirements of subclause 457.223(2) or (4) (as in force before 18 March 2018):
(a)the holder:

(B)if the sponsor is, or was, a standard business sponsor who was lawfully operating a business in Australia at the time of the sponsor’s approval as a standard business sponsor, or at the time of the last approval of a variation to the sponsor’s term of approval as a standard business sponsor—must work only in a position in the business of the sponsor or an associated entity of the sponsor; or

(C)if the sponsor is or was a standard business sponsor who was not lawfully operating a business in Australia, and was lawfully operating a business outside Australia, at the time of the sponsor’s approval as a standard business sponsor, or at the time of the last approval of a variation to the sponsor’s term of approval as a standard business sponsor—must work only in a position in the business of the sponsor; and
(aa)subject to paragraph (c), the holder must:
(i)if the holder was outside Australia when the visa was granted—commence work within 90 days after the holder’s arrival in Australia; and
(ii)if the holder was in Australia when the visa was granted—commence work within 90 days after the holder’s visa was granted; and
(b)the holder may cease to work in accordance with paragraph (a) for a period, but:
(i)any such period must not exceed 180 consecutive days; and
(ii)the total number of days on which the holder does not work in accordance with paragraph (a) must not exceed 365 during the visa period for the holder’s visa; and

(c)if the holder is required to hold a licence, registration or membership that is mandatory to perform the occupation nominated in relation to the holder, in the location where the holder’s position is situated—the holder:
(i)must hold the licence, registration or membership while the holder is performing the occupation; and
(ii)if the holder was outside Australia when the visa was granted—the holder must hold that licence, registration or membership within 90 days after the holder’s arrival in Australia; and
(iii)if the holder was in Australia when the visa was granted—the holder must hold that licence, registration or membership within 90 days after the holder’s visa was granted; and
(iv)must notify the Department, in writing as soon as practicable if an application for the licence, registration or membership is refused; and
(v)must comply with each condition or requirement to which the licence, registration or membership is subject; and

(vi)must not engage in work that is inconsistent with the licence, registration or membership, including any conditions or requirements to which the licence, registration or membership is subject; and
(vii)must notify the Department, in writing as soon as practicable if the licence, registration or membership ceases to be in force or is revoked or cancelled.
(3A)For subparagraph (3)(a)(ii), the circumstances are that:
(a)the holder’s occupation is specified in an instrument in writing for subparagraph 2.72(10)(e)(ii) or (iii) as in force before 18 March 2018; or

(b)the holder is continuing to work for the sponsor, or the associated entity of the sponsor, for the purpose of fulfilling a requirement under a law relating to industrial relations and relating to the giving of notice.
(4)If the visa is:
(a)a Subclass 401 (Temporary Work (Long Stay Activity)) visa; or
(b)a Subclass 402 (Training and Research) visa; or
(ba)a Subclass 420 (Temporary Work (Entertainment)) visa;
the holder must not:
(c)cease to engage in the most recently nominated occupation, program or activity in relation to which the holder is identified; or
(d)engage in work or an activity that is inconsistent with the most recently nominated occupation, program or activity in relation to which the holder is identified; or

(e)engage in work or an activity for an employer other than the employer identified in accordance with paragraph 2.72A(7)(a) as in force before 19 November 2016 (subject to subregulation 2.72A(8) as in force before that day) in the most recent nomination in which the holder is identified.
(5)If the visa is a subclass 407 (Training) visa, the holder must not:
(a)cease to engage in the most recently nominated program in relation to which the holder is identified; or
(b)engage in work or an activity that is inconsistent with the most recently nominated program in relation to which the holder is identified; or

(c)engage in work or an activity for an employer other than an employer identified in accordance with paragraph 2.72A(8)(a) (subject to subregulation 2.72A(9)) in the most recent nomination in which the holder is identified.
conditions.dha_web_title: 8107 - Work limitation
conditions.dha_web_summary:
The visa  you hold was granted to either allow you to be employed by a particular  employer, or to undertake specific activities in Australia.
If employed, you must not stop working for your employer. You  must not work in a different position, occupation, with another employer, or  for yourself
You must not stop doing the activity the visa was granted for
You must not do other activities that are not related to the  activity the visa was granted for.
Note:  For information on how condition 8107 applies to Subclass 408 Pandemic Event visa  holders, go to
Temporary  Activity visa (subclass 408) Australian Government endorsed events (COVID-19  Pandemic event).
For  information on how condition 8107 applies to Subclass 408 Workplace Justice  visa holders, go to
Temporary  Activity visa (subclass 408) Australian Government Endorsed Events (Workplace  Justice Pilot).
Subclass 457
If  you hold a Subclass 457 visa, or it was your last substantive visa, you must
only work in the occupation listed in your most recently  approved nomination​
only work for the sponsor who nominated the position you are  working in. (If your sponsor is a standard business sponsor and is an  Australian business, you can also work for an associated entity of the sponsor)
hold a licence, registration or membership if it is mandatory to  perform the occupation for which you were nominated.
If  you hold a Subclass 457 visa, or it was your last substantive visa, and your  employment with your sponsor ends, you can stop working or work outside of the  above conditions for a limited time:
up to 180 days in       a single period
up to 365 days in       total across the period your visa is granted for.
These  time periods start from 1 July 2024. They do not include any earlier periods of  time when you stopped working under the condition in place before that date.
You  must start work within 90 days of:
arriving in       Australia, if you were outside Australia when the visa was granted
being granted your       visa, if you were in Australia when the visa was granted.
For more information on how condition 8107  applies to Subclass 457 visa holders, see
Temporary  Work (Skilled) visa (subclass 457).​
Understanding your work rights
The  Department is working with the Fair Work Ombudsman to help employees and  employers understand and follow Australian Workplace laws.
Information  on pay rates, shift calculations, leave arrangements and notice and redundancy  entitlements is in the
Pay and Conditions Tool (PACT).
The  Fair Work Ombudsman website has more information on workplace rights and  entitlements for
visa  holders and migrant workers.
For  the full list of conditions relevant to your visa, see the
Federal Register of  Legislation.​

(c)must not engage in work for another person or on the holder’s own account while undertaking the employment in relation to which the visa was granted; and
(d)must not cease to be employed by the employer in relation to which the visa was granted, unless paragraph (e) applies; and
(e)except with the written permission of the Foreign Minister, must not remain in Australia after the permanent departure of that employer.
conditions.dha_web_title: 8110 - Work Limitation
conditions.dha_web_summary:
You must not:
work in Australia except in the household of the employer in  relation to whom the visa was granted
work in a position or occupation inconsistent  with the position or occupation in relation to which the visa was granted
work for another person or yourself while undertaking the employment in relation to which the visa was granted
cease to be employed by the employer in  relation to which the visa was granted, and
remain in Australia after the permanent departure of that employer from Australia.
If you want to stay in Australia after your employer leaves Australia, you must get written permission from the
Australian Minister for Foreign Affairs.
Understanding your work rights
The Department is working with the Fair Work Ombudsman to help employees and employers understand and follow Australian Workplace laws.
Information on pay rates, shift calculations, leave arrangements and notice and redundancy entitlements is in the
Pay and Conditions Tool (PACT).
The Fair Work Ombudsman website has more information on workplace rights and entitlements for
visa holders and migrant workers.
For the full list of conditions relevant to your visa, see the Federal Register of Legislation.

conditions.title_ko: 스폰서 가사 전용 근무 및 스폰서 영구 출국 후 잔류 금지
conditions.title_en: Work Only in Sponsor's Household & Depart With Sponsor
conditions.summary_ko: 8110과 유사하게 스폰서 고용주의 가정 내에서만 근로해야 하며, 스폰서가 호주를 영구히 떠나면 더 이상 호주에 머물 수 없습니다.
conditions.summary_en: You must work solely in your sponsor's household and must not remain in Australia after the sponsor permanently departs.
forbidden_ko: 스폰서 가정(household) 외부에서의 일체의 근로
스폰서 영구 출국 이후 호주 내 체류 지속
forbidden_en: Any work outside the sponsor's household
Remaining in Australia after the sponsor permanently leaves
obligations_ko: 스폰서 가정 전속 근로 및 스폰서 영구 귀국·출국 시 비자 기간과 무관하게 출국
obligations_en: Work exclusively in the sponsor's household and depart when they depart permanently
exceptions_ko: 조문상 외교부 장관 예외조차 두지 않은 엄격한 금지 조항입니다.
exceptions_en: No exceptions listed within clause 8111.
conditions.waiver_ko: 별도 예외 조항이 없으므로 타 비자로 전환하거나 출국해야 합니다.
conditions.waiver_en: No built-in waiver.

clause_notes_ko.text: 8110보다 간결하며 스폰서 가사 근로 및 영구 출국 시 체류 종료를 규정합니다.

clause_notes_en.text: Prohibits non-household work and post-departure stay.

conditions.statutory_text:
8111The holder must not:
(a)perform work in Australia except in the household of the employer who is the holder’s sponsor in relation to the visa; or
(b)remain in Australia after the permanent departure of that employer.
statutory_paragraphs: 8111The holder must not:
(a)perform work in Australia except in the household of the employer who is the holder’s sponsor in relation to the visa; or
(b)remain in Australia after the permanent departure of that employer.
conditions.dha_web_title: 8111 - Work limitation
conditions.dha_web_summary:
You cannot work in Australia except in the household of the visa holder's sponsor.
You cannot stay in Australia once the sponsor has permanently left Australia.
Understanding your work rights
The Department is working with the Fair Work Ombudsman to help employees and employers understand and follow Australian Workplace laws.
Information on pay rates, shift calculations, leave arrangements and notice and redundancy entitlements is in the

The Fair Work Ombudsman website has more information on workplace rights and entitlements for

conditions.title_ko: 호주 시민·영주권자 대체 가능 근로 금지
conditions.title_en: No Work That an Australian Citizen or PR Might Otherwise Do
conditions.summary_ko: 호주 시민권자나 영주권자가 수행할 수 있는 일반 일자리를 대신 차지하는 형태의 근로가 금지됩니다(퇴직·특수 비자 등).
conditions.summary_en: You must not engage in work in Australia that might otherwise be carried out by an Australian citizen or permanent resident.
forbidden_ko: 호주 내 일반 노동시장에서 호주 시민·영주권자를 고용해 처리할 수 있는 직무·근로 일체
forbidden_en: Any employment or work role that could reasonably be filled by an Australian citizen or permanent resident
obligations_ko: 단순 해외 자산 관리·자문 또는 본인 고유 사업의 비대체적 활동 범위 준수
obligations_en: Avoid local employment or contracting roles competing with Australian workers
exceptions_ko: 조문상 예외 문구 없음 (순수 비고용 활동만 가능)
exceptions_en: No statutory carve-out in clause 8112.
conditions.waiver_ko: 임시 퇴직비자(405/410)나 구 브리징 비자 승계 등에서 주로 등장합니다.
conditions.waiver_en: Not waivable; general work rights require a visa without 8112.

clause_notes_ko.text: 해외 본사 파견 등 특수 목적이나 퇴직 비자 등에서 내국인 고용시장 침해를 막기 위해 사용됩니다.

clause_notes_en.text: Protects local labour market access by barring work replaceable by citizens/PRs.

conditions.statutory_text: 8112The holder must not engage in work in Australia that might otherwise be carried out by an Australian citizen or an Australian permanent resident.
statutory_paragraphs: 8112The holder must not engage in work in Australia that might otherwise be carried out by an Australian citizen or an Australian permanent resident.
conditions.dha_web_title: 8112 - Must not engage in work that might otherwise be carried out by an Australian citizen or permanent resident
conditions.dha_web_summary:
You cannot perform work in Australia that an Australian citizen or permanent resident could do.
Understanding your work rights
The Department is working with the Fair Work Ombudsman to help employees and employers understand and follow Australian Workplace laws.
Information on pay rates, shift calculations, leave arrangements and notice and redundancy entitlements is in the

conditions.title_ko: 비군용 선박 승무원 외 근로 금지 (해상승무원)
conditions.title_en: Work Only as Crew of Non-Military Ship
conditions.summary_ko: 호주 내에서 비군용 선박(상선 등)의 승무원(crew member)으로서의 업무 외에는 일할 수 없습니다.
conditions.summary_en: You must not work in Australia other than as a crew member of a non-military ship.
forbidden_ko: 육상 일반 취업, 하선 후 아르바이트, 군용 선박 관련 근로
forbidden_en: Any onshore employment or work outside crew duties on a non-military vessel
obligations_ko: 선원 비자(Maritime Crew 988 등) 목적에 부합하는 승무원 직무만 수행
obligations_en: Perform only duties as crew of a non-military ship
exceptions_ko: 없음
exceptions_en: None.
conditions.waiver_ko: 육상 근로를 하려면 별도 육상 취업 비자가 필요합니다.
conditions.waiver_en: Requires a separate onshore work visa.

clause_notes_ko.text: 해상 승무원 전용 근로 제한 조항입니다.

clause_notes_en.text: Restricts work exclusively to non-military ship crew duties.

conditions.statutory_text: 8113The holder must not work in Australia otherwise than as a member of the crew of a nonmilitary ship.
statutory_paragraphs: 8113The holder must not work in Australia otherwise than as a member of the crew of a nonmilitary ship.
conditions.dha_web_title: 8113 - Not to work other than as crew member of non-military ship
conditions.dha_web_summary:
You can only work in Australia as a crew member of a non-military ship.
Understanding your work rights
The Department is working with the Fair Work Ombudsman to help employees and employers understand and follow Australian Workplace laws.
Information on pay rates, shift calculations, leave arrangements and notice and redundancy entitlements is in the
Pay and Conditions Tool (PACT).

visa holders and migrant workers.

conditions.title_ko: 슈퍼요트 승무원 외 근로 금지
conditions.title_en: Work Only as Superyacht Crew
conditions.summary_ko: 슈퍼요트(superyacht) 승무원으로서의 업무 외에는 호주에서 어떤 근로도 할 수 없습니다.
conditions.summary_en: You must not work in Australia otherwise than as a crew member of a superyacht.
forbidden_ko: 일반 육상 취업, 상선·일반 관광선 등 슈퍼요트 승무와 무관한 근로
forbidden_en: Any work other than superyacht crew duties
obligations_ko: 승선 중인 슈퍼요트 승무원 직무만 수행
obligations_en: Restrict all work in Australia to superyacht crew duties
exceptions_ko: 없음
exceptions_en: None.
conditions.waiver_ko: 육상 취업 시 다른 비자를 받아야 합니다.
conditions.waiver_en: Separate visa required for onshore work.

clause_notes_ko.text: Subclass 408(슈퍼요트) 및 구 488에 적용됩니다.

clause_notes_en.text: Applies to superyacht crew arrangements (e.g., Subclass 408 / legacy 488).

conditions.statutory_text: 8114The holder must not work in Australia otherwise than as a member of the crew of a superyacht.
statutory_paragraphs: 8114The holder must not work in Australia otherwise than as a member of the crew of a superyacht.
conditions.dha_web_title: 8114 - Superyacht crew
conditions.dha_web_summary:
You can only work in Australia as a member of the crew of a superyacht.
Understanding your work rights

conditions.title_ko: 상용 방문 활동 외 근로 금지 (ETA 601 · eVisitor 651 · 600 상용)
conditions.title_en: Business Visitor Activities Only (No Paid Local Work)
conditions.summary_ko: ETA(601), eVisitor(651), 600 상용방문 비자에 붙는 조건으로, 회의·계약 협상·시장 조사 같은 'Business Visitor Activity'만 허용되고 호주 내 취업·용역 제공은 금지됩니다.
conditions.summary_en: You may only undertake genuine business visitor activities (meetings, negotiations, conferences) and must not work for an Australian business or sell goods/services directly to the public.
forbidden_ko: 호주 회사에 고용되거나 호주 고객에게 직접 유료 서비스·노무를 제공하는 행위
소매 판매, 현장 시공·수리 등 일반 근로 활동
forbidden_en: Taking employment in Australia, supplying services to an Australian business/entity, or selling directly to the Australian public
obligations_ko: 계약 협상·비즈니스 미팅·콘퍼런스 참석·일반 사업 문의(reg 1.03 Business Visitor Activity) 범위만 유지
obligations_en: Limit activities strictly to business inquiries, contract negotiations, and conferences
exceptions_ko: 법정 정의(reg 1.03)상의 상용 방문 활동만 허용(특수 단기 전문기술 파견이 필요하면 Subclass 400 검토)
exceptions_en: Permitted business visitor activities under reg 1.03 (hands-on specialist work requires a Subclass 400 or work visa)
conditions.waiver_ko: 웨이버 규정이 없으므로 단기 기술 지원·설치·유료 업무를 하려면 입국 전 Subclass 400 등을 신청해야 합니다.
conditions.waiver_en: No waiver; hands-on specialist work requires applying for Subclass 400 or 482.

clause_notes_ko.text: 한국 여권자들이 많이 쓰는 ETA(601)로 호주 거래처 회의는 가능하지만, 호주 현장에서 장비를 직접 설치하거나 일하면 8115 위반(공항 입국 취소 포함)이 됩니다.

clause_notes_en.text: Common on ETA (601), eVisitor (651), and 600 Business Visitor visas—allows meetings/negotiations but prohibits hands-on operational work.

scenarios.q_ko: ETA(601)로 들어와서 거래처 장비 설치나 A/S 작업을 며칠만 해주는 것도 안 되나요?
scenarios.q_en: Can I enter on an ETA (601) to install or repair client equipment for a few days?
scenarios.a_ko: 위반 위험이 매우 높습니다. 실제 기술 작업이나 현장 작업은 '상용 방문 활동(business visitor activity)'을 벗어나므로 단기 전문활동 비자(Subclass 400)를 받아 입국해야 안전합니다.
scenarios.a_en: High breach risk. Hands-on installation or technical servicing normally falls outside 'business visitor activity' and requires a Subclass 400 (Temporary Work - Short Stay Specialist) visa.

conditions.statutory_text: 8115The holder must not work in Australia other than by engaging in a business visitor activity.
statutory_paragraphs: 8115The holder must not work in Australia other than by engaging in a business visitor activity.
conditions.dha_web_title: 8115 - Limited activities
conditions.dha_web_summary:
The holder must not work in Australia other than by engaging in a business visitor activity.
You can:
make general business or employment enquiries
investigate, negotiate, sign or review business contracts
undertake an activity of an official government-to-government visit
participate in conferences, trade fairs or seminars in Australia—but the organisers must not pay you for taking part
You must not:
undertake work for, or supply services to, an organisation or other person based in Australia
sell goods or services directly to the general public

conditions.title_ko: 장관 고시 지정 활동 외 근로 금지 (특정 BVE 등)
conditions.title_en: Specified Legislative Instrument Activities Only
conditions.summary_ko: 장관이 입법고시(Legislative Instrument)로 지정한 특정 직종·활동 외의 근로는 일체 금지됩니다.
conditions.summary_en: You must not work in Australia except in an activity specified by the Minister in a legislative instrument for this clause.
forbidden_ko: 입법고시에 명시되지 않은 모든 직무 및 일반 취업
forbidden_en: Any work outside the activities specified in the Minister's legislative instrument
obligations_ko: 현행 고시 대상 활동인지 확인 후 해당 범위 내에서만 근무
obligations_en: Verify your intended work falls within the current legislative instrument before starting
exceptions_ko: 고시된 특정 활동만 허용
exceptions_en: Activities listed in the ministerial instrument
conditions.waiver_ko: 브리징 비자 등에서 조건 변경 또는 신규 비자 발급으로만 전환 가능합니다.
conditions.waiver_en: Requires a different visa or condition-free grant.

clause_notes_ko.text: 주로 050 브리징 비자(BVE)나 특정 임시 체류자에게 제한된 산업·활동만 열어줄 때 사용됩니다.

clause_notes_en.text: Restricts BVE/selected temporary holders strictly to instrument-specified work.

conditions.statutory_text: 8116The holder must not work in Australia other than by engaging in an activity specified in a legislative instrument made by the Minister for this clause.
statutory_paragraphs: 8116The holder must not work in Australia other than by engaging in an activity specified in a legislative instrument made by the Minister for this clause.
conditions.dha_web_title: 8116 - Specified work only
conditions.dha_web_summary:
You must not work in Australia other than as a crew member on either or both of the following:
the flight on which you leave Australia
one flight from a proclaimed airport to the proclaimed airport from which you leave Australia

conditions.title_ko: 항공사 대기 승무원 출국편 제한 (Positioning Crew)
conditions.title_en: Airline Positioning Crew — Outbound Flight Work Only
conditions.summary_ko: 항공기 편승(positioning) 승무원이 호주를 떠나는 항공편(또는 출국 공항으로 이동하는 국내선 1편)의 승무원 임무 외 다른 근로를 금지합니다.
conditions.summary_en: Restricts work solely to crew duties on the departing international flight and one connecting domestic flight to the departure airport.
forbidden_ko: 지정 출국편·연결편 외 항공사 지상 근무나 일반 취업 일체
forbidden_en: Any work outside the specified outbound international flight or connecting departure flight
obligations_ko: (a) 호주 출국편 및 (b) 공항 간 이동 연결편(1회)에서의 승무원 임무만 수행
obligations_en: Work only as crew on the outbound flight (a) or one connecting flight to the departure airport (b)
exceptions_ko: 없음
exceptions_en: None.
conditions.waiver_ko: 특수목적비자(reg 2.40A) 연계 항공 승무원 전용 조항입니다.
conditions.waiver_en: Specific to airline positioning crew.

clause_notes_ko.text: 특수목적비자(Special Purpose Visa)로 입국하는 편승 항공 승무원을 위한 규정입니다.

clause_notes_en.text: Applies to airline positioning crew under reg 2.40A.

statutory_paragraphs: 8117The holder must not work in Australia other than as a member of the crew on either or both of the following:
(a)the flight on which the holder leaves Australia;
(b)one flight from a proclaimed airport to the proclaimed airport from which the holder leaves Australia.
conditions.dha_web_title: 8117 - Work Limitation – Airline positioning crew
conditions.dha_web_summary:
You must not work in Australia other than as a crew member on either or both of the following:
the flight on which you leave Australia
one flight from a proclaimed airport to the proclaimed airport from which you leave Australia

conditions.title_ko: 항공사 현업 승무원 입·출국편 제한 (Airline Crew)
conditions.title_en: Airline Crew — Inbound/Outbound Flight Work Only
conditions.summary_ko: 항공기 운항 승무원이 호주 입국편, 입국 공항 간 연결편 1회, 출국편, 출국 공항 간 연결편 1회 외 다른 근로를 하는 것을 금지합니다.
conditions.summary_en: Restricts work solely to crew duties on the inbound/outbound flights and at most one connecting domestic sector on entry and departure.
forbidden_ko: 지정 운항 편성 외 육상 일반 취업 또는 장기 국내선 순환 근무
forbidden_en: Any work other than crew duties on the inbound/outbound sectors and permitted domestic positioning legs
obligations_ko: (a)~(d)에 열거된 입·출국 및 공항 간 연결 항공편 승무원 임무만 수행
obligations_en: Perform crew duties strictly on sectors (a)–(d)
exceptions_ko: 없음
exceptions_en: None.
conditions.waiver_ko: 특수목적비자(reg 2.40A) 항공 승무원 전용 조항입니다.
conditions.waiver_en: Specific to airline crew.

clause_notes_ko.text: 8117과 달리 입국편((a)-(b))과 출국편((c)-(d))을 모두 포함합니다.

clause_notes_en.text: Covers both inbound and outbound sectors plus one domestic transfer each way.

statutory_paragraphs: 8118The holder must not work in Australia other than as a member of the crew on one or more of the following:
(a)the flight on which the holder travels to Australia;
(b)one flight from the proclaimed airport at which the holder enters Australia to another proclaimed airport;
(c)the flight on which the holder leaves Australia;
(d)one flight from a proclaimed airport to the proclaimed airport from which the holder leaves Australia.
conditions.dha_web_title: 8118 - Work Limitation – Airline Crew
conditions.dha_web_summary:
You must not work in Australia other than as a  member of the crew of one or more of the following:
the flight on which you travel to Australia
one flight from the proclaimed airport at which you enter Australia to another proclaimed airport
the flight on which you leave Australia
one flight from a proclaimed airport to the proclaimed airport from which you leave Australia

conditions.title_ko: 최대 3개월 이내 학업·연수 제한
conditions.title_en: Maximum 3 Months Study or Training
conditions.summary_ko: 호주 체류 중 총 3개월(약 12주)을 초과하여 어떤 학업이나 직업훈련(어학연수 포함)도 수강할 수 없습니다.
conditions.summary_en: While in Australia, you must not study or undertake training for more than 3 months in total.
forbidden_ko: 어학원·대학·직업학교(VET)·단기 자격과정 등 총합 3개월 초과 등록 및 수강
forbidden_en: Engaging in studies or training exceeding 3 months in Australia
obligations_ko: 어학연수나 단기 수업을 들을 경우 전체 수료 기간이 3개월 이내인지 사전에 확인
obligations_en: Keep cumulative study or training within 3 months while on this visa
exceptions_ko: (2) 테이블 1: 590 가디언 비자 소지자의 주당 20시간 미만 ELICOS(어학연수) 수강은 3개월 초과 허용
(2) 테이블 1A/2/3: 만 18세 미만 의료치료비자(602/675/685) 소지자가 호주 내 사정 변경으로 장관 서면 허가를 받은 경우
exceptions_en: (2) Item 1: Subclass 590 Student Guardian undertaking ELICOS of less than 20 hours/week
(2) Items 1A/2/3: Under-18 medical treatment holders (602/675/685) with written ministerial permission due to changed circumstances
conditions.waiver_ko: 3개월 이상 정규 학업을 원하면 학생비자(Subclass 500) 등 학업이 허용되는 비자로 전환해야 합니다(단, 8503/8534 등 제한 유무 확인 필수).
conditions.waiver_en: Requires a visa permitting longer study (such as Subclass 500, subject to any 8503/further-stay bar).

clause_notes_ko.text: 관광비자(600), ETA(601), eVisitor(651), 학생비자 18세 이상 동반가족(500.612(1)(c)), 590 가디언 등에 널리 붙습니다.
590 학생 가디언 비자 부모님은 주당 20시간 미만 조건을 지키면 3개월 이상 어학원(ELICOS)을 다닐 수 있습니다.

clause_notes_en.text: Applies across Visitor (600/601/651), adult Student dependants, and Student Guardians.
Carves out ELICOS under 20 hrs/week for Subclass 590 Guardians and approved under-18 medical treatment cases.

scenarios.q_ko: 관광비자(600)나 ETA(601)로 3개월 이상 어학연수를 하면서 코스만 쪼개 등록하면 괜찮나요?
scenarios.q_en: Can I enrol in back-to-back short courses exceeding 3 months in total on a Visitor/ETA visa?
scenarios.a_ko: 안 됩니다. 코스를 나눠 등록해도 호주 체류 중 총 학업·연수 기간이 3개월을 넘으면 8201 위반입니다.
scenarios.a_en: No. Splitting courses does not reset the 3-month total limit; total study/training while in Australia cannot exceed 3 months.

conditions.dha_web_title: 8201 - Maximum 3 months study
conditions.dha_web_summary:
While in Australia, you must not engage, for more than 3 months, in any studies or training.
See the Regulations
conditions.dha_web_scenario:
In certain circumstances, this restriction does not apply to:
subclass 590 (Student Guardian) visas
subclass 602 (Medical Treatment) visas
subclass 675 (Medical Treatment (Short Stay)) visas
subclass 685 (Medical Treatment (Long Stay)) visas
Subclass 590 visa holders
You can study up to 20 hours a week on an English Language Intensive Course for Overseas Students (ELICOS).
Subclass 602, 675 and 685 visa holders
You may study in Australia for more than 3 months if:
you are under 18
your circumstances have changed while in Australia
you have written permission to do so because of your circumstances
Other visa holders
You must not study or train in Australia for more than 3 months in total.
For the full list of conditions relevant to your visa, see the
Federal Register of Legislation.

conditions.title_ko: 학생비자 학업 유지·코스레벨(AQF)·출석/성적 의무
conditions.title_en: Student Course Enrolment, AQF Level, Progress & Attendance
conditions.summary_ko: 학생비자(500)의 핵심 조건으로, 풀타임 등록 과정(CoE) 유지, 승인 당시와 동급 이상 AQF 학위 유지(단 박사→석사는 허용), 성적·출석 미달 제재 없음 요건을 모두 지켜야 합니다.
conditions.summary_en: Core Subclass 500 condition: stay enrolled in a full-time registered course at the same or higher AQF level (except PhD to Masters downgrade permitted) and maintain satisfactory course progress and attendance.
forbidden_ko: 등록 과정(CoE) 취소 후 무등록 방치 또는 파트타임 축소
승인 당시 학위보다 낮은 AQF 레벨 과정으로 무단 하향 이동 (예: 학사 AQF 7 → 디플로마 AQF 5)
학교가 ESOS Act s 19에 따라 성적 불량 또는 출석률 미달로 이민성 보고(certification) 확정
forbidden_en: Allowing your CoE to cancel without holding a valid full-time enrolment
Downgrading to a lower AQF level course (e.g., Bachelor AQF 7 to Diploma AQF 5) without obtaining a new Subclass 500 visa
Receiving a certified failure of course progress or attendance under ESOS Act s 19
obligations_ko: (2)(a) 풀타임 CRICOS 등록 과정 상시 유지
(2)(b) 기존 비자 승인 과정과 동급 이상(AQF) 과정 유지
(2)(c) 성적(progress) 및 출석률(attendance) 기준 충족
obligations_en: (2)(a) Remain enrolled in a full-time registered course
(2)(b) Maintain same or higher AQF level
(2)(c) Avoid s 19 non-satisfactory progress/attendance certification
exceptions_ko: (3) 박사(AQF 10) 등록 학생이 석사(AQF 9) 과정으로 변경하는 경우만 새 비자 없이 8202(2)(b) 충족 간주
2016년 7월 이후 '28일 초과 휴학 시 자동 취소' 규정은 존재하지 않으나, CoE 취소 통보 후 s 116 취소 심사의 대상이 되므로 즉시 유효한 CoE 확보 필요
exceptions_en: (3) Downgrading from AQF Level 10 (Doctorate) to AQF Level 9 (Masters) is expressly permitted under 8202(3)
There is no automatic 28-day cancellation—cancellation still requires an s 116 process and NOICC, though losing CoE puts the visa at immediate risk
conditions.waiver_ko: 단순 하향 변경(예: 대학→VET)은 웨이버가 없으므로 새 학생비자(500)를 받아야 하며, 이미 성적·출석 미달이나 CoE 취소로 NOICC를 받았다면 5영업일 소명이 필수입니다.
conditions.waiver_en: Downgrading AQF levels (other than PhD→Masters) requires a new Subclass 500 visa; if a NOICC issues, respond within 5 working days.

clause_notes_ko.text: 항상 CRICOS에 등록된 풀타임 과정에 등록돼 있어야 합니다.
최초 비자 승인 시의 AQF 레벨 이상을 유지해야 합니다. 다만 박사(AQF 10)→석사(AQF 9) 변경만 조문 (3)항으로 예외 인정됩니다.
학교 내부 경고 단계가 아니라 교육기관이 ESOS법 제19조에 따라 '불만족'으로 공식 인증(certify)해 보고한 경우 8202 위반이 성립합니다.

clause_notes_en.text: Must maintain enrolment in a full-time registered CRICOS course.
Requires same or higher AQF level, with a statutory carve-out in (3) only for AQF 10 → AQF 9.
Breach is triggered when the provider certifies unsatisfactory progress or attendance under ESOS Act s 19.

scenarios.q_ko: 학교를 옮기거나 휴학해 CoE가 취소되면 28일 뒤 비자가 자동으로 취소되나요?
scenarios.q_en: Does a cancelled CoE automatically cancel my visa after 28 days?
scenarios.a_ko: 자동 취소는 아닙니다. 다만 8202(2)(a) 위반 상태가 되어 이민성이 취소 예고(NOICC)를 보낼 법적 근거(s 116(1)(b))가 생기므로, 빠르게 새 CoE를 받거나 합당한 사유·증빙을 갖추어야 합니다.
scenarios.a_en: No automatic cancellation occurs, but without an active full-time CoE you breach 8202(2)(a), exposing your visa to an s 116 NOICC unless resolved promptly.

conditions.statutory_text:
8202(1)The holder must be enrolled in a fulltime course of study or training if the holder is:
(a)a Defence student; or
(b)a Foreign Affairs student; or
(c)a secondary exchange student.
(2)A holder not covered by subclause (1):
(a)must be enrolled in a fulltime registered course; and
(b)subject to subclause (3), must maintain enrolment in a registered course that, once completed, will provide a qualification from the Australian Qualifications Framework that is at the same level as, or at a higher level than, the registered course in relation to which the visa was granted; and
(c)must ensure that neither of the following subparagraphs applies in respect of a registered course undertaken by the holder:
(i)the education provider has certified the holder, for a registered course undertaken by the holder, as not achieving satisfactory course progress for section 19 of the Education Services for Overseas Students Act 2000 and the relevant standard of the national code made by the Education Minister under section 33 of that Act;
(ii)the education provider has certified the holder, for a registered course undertaken by the holder, as not achieving satisfactory course attendance for section 19 of the Education Services for Overseas Students Act 2000 and the relevant standard of the national code made by the Education Minister under section 33 of that Act.
(3)A holder is taken to satisfy the requirement set out in paragraph (2)(b) if the holder:
(a)is enrolled in a course at the Australian Qualifications Framework level 10; and
(b)changes their enrolment to a course at the Australian Qualifications Framework level 9.
statutory_paragraphs: 8202(1)The holder must be enrolled in a fulltime course of study or training if the holder is:
(a)a Defence student; or
(b)a Foreign Affairs student; or
(c)a secondary exchange student.
(2)A holder not covered by subclause (1):
(a)must be enrolled in a fulltime registered course; and

(b)subject to subclause (3), must maintain enrolment in a registered course that, once completed, will provide a qualification from the Australian Qualifications Framework that is at the same level as, or at a higher level than, the registered course in relation to which the visa was granted; and
(c)must ensure that neither of the following subparagraphs applies in respect of a registered course undertaken by the holder:

(i)the education provider has certified the holder, for a registered course undertaken by the holder, as not achieving satisfactory course progress for section 19 of the Education Services for Overseas Students Act 2000 and the relevant standard of the national code made by the Education Minister under section 33 of that Act;

(ii)the education provider has certified the holder, for a registered course undertaken by the holder, as not achieving satisfactory course attendance for section 19 of the Education Services for Overseas Students Act 2000 and the relevant standard of the national code made by the Education Minister under section 33 of that Act.
(3)A holder is taken to satisfy the requirement set out in paragraph (2)(b) if the holder:
(a)is enrolled in a course at the Australian Qualifications Framework level 10; and
(b)changes their enrolment to a course at the Australian Qualifications Framework level 9.
conditions.dha_web_title: 8202 - Meet course requirements
conditions.dha_web_summary:
You must:
remain enrolled in a registered course  (if you are a Foreign Affairs or Defence sponsored student or a secondary exchange student you must maintain full-time enrolment in your course of study or training)
maintain enrolment in a registered course that is the same
Australian Qualifications Framework (AQF) level or higher for which we granted your student visa, unless changing from AQF level 10 to level 9. See:
Change in study situation.
maintain satisfactory attendance in your course and course progress for each study period as required by your education provider.
Note: A registered course is one that is on the
Commonwealth Register of Institutions and Courses for Overseas Students (CRICOS).
Gap between courses
Generally course gaps should not be more 2 months. A course gap can be more than 2 months if:
it is the end of the academic year study break
you are affected by
education provider default
you have completed your course and you are applying for a new visa

conditions.title_ko: 국가안보 평가 없이 학업·논문 주제 변경 금지 (특정 국적·과정)
conditions.title_en: No Course or Thesis Change Without Security Approval
conditions.summary_ko: 호주 관계 당국의 국가안보 위험 평가를 거쳐 이민성 장관의 승인을 받기 전까지는 학업 과정이나 논문·연구 주제를 변경할 수 없습니다.
conditions.summary_en: You must not change your course of study, thesis, or research topic without ministerial approval following a national security assessment.
forbidden_ko: 장관의 사전 안보 심사 승인 없이 전공·코스·석박사 논문·연구 주제 변경
forbidden_en: Changing your course, thesis, or research topic without prior ministerial approval
obligations_ko: 전공이나 연구 주제 변경 전 이민성 승인 신청 및 안보 심사 완료 대기
obligations_en: Obtain written approval from the Minister before switching courses or research topics
exceptions_ko: 최초 비자 승인 시 등록된 기존 과정·연구 주제를 그대로 유지하는 경우
exceptions_en: Continuing the initially approved course and research topic
conditions.waiver_ko: cl 500.611(1)(b) 등에 따라 특정 국적(예: 이란 시민권자 고등교육·연구과정)에 강제 적용되며, 임의 변경 시 즉시 위반이 됩니다.
conditions.waiver_en: Mandatory for specific profiles (e.g., Iranian citizens in higher education/postgrad research under cl 500.611(1)(b)); requires prior ministerial approval to vary.

clause_notes_ko.text: 8204(대학원 과정 자체 진입 제한)와 달리, 이미 다니는 과정·논문·연구 주제를 바꿀 때 안보 평가를 거치도록 요구합니다.

clause_notes_en.text: Requires security clearance and ministerial approval prior to changing an existing course, thesis, or research topic.

conditions.statutory_text: 8203The holder must not change his or her course of study, or thesis or research topic, unless approval is given by the Minister after the Minister has obtained an assessment from the competent Australian authorities that the holder is not likely to be directly or indirectly a risk to Australian national security.
statutory_paragraphs: 8203The holder must not change his or her course of study, or thesis or research topic, unless approval is given by the Minister after the Minister has obtained an assessment from the competent Australian authorities that the holder is not likely to be directly or indirectly a risk to Australian national security.
conditions.dha_web_title: 8203 - Limited study change
conditions.dha_web_summary:
You must not change your course of study, thesis or research topic without the approval of the Minister.-
This approval can only be given after the Minister has obtained an assessment from the competent Australian authorities that you are not likely to be directly or indirectly a risk to Australian national security.
If you are considering changing your thesis, major or research topic you must: complete
Form 1221 - Additional personal particulars information (PDF) and ​submit a
8203/8204 Change of Study Assessment Request​.
See the regulation​​​

conditions.title_ko: 국가안보 평가 없이 대학원·석박사 과정 수강·변경 금지
conditions.title_en: No Graduate/Masters/PhD Course or Research Without Security Approval
conditions.summary_ko: 관계 당국의 국가안보 평가 및 장관 승인 없이는 Graduate Certificate/Diploma, 석사·박사 과정 또는 그 예비 과정(bridging course)을 새로 수강하거나 변경할 수 없습니다.
conditions.summary_en: You must not undertake or change a Graduate Certificate, Graduate Diploma, Masters, Doctorate, or prerequisite bridging course without ministerial security approval.
forbidden_ko: (a) 준석사(Grad Cert/Dip)·석사·박사 과정 및 (b) 그 선행 브리징 코스를 장관 승인 없이 수강 또는 변경
forbidden_en: Undertaking or changing a Grad Cert/Dip, Masters, PhD, or prerequisite bridging course without prior security approval
obligations_ko: 고등 학위 또는 연구 과정 진학·변경 전 이민성 사전 승인 요청
obligations_en: Obtain ministerial approval before commencing or changing postgraduate study/research
exceptions_ko: 학부·직업교육(VET) 이하 과정 유지 또는 장관 승인 완료 후 수강
exceptions_en: Non-postgraduate study or study approved after security assessment
conditions.waiver_ko: 특정 국적(cl 500.611(1)(c), 500.612(1)(d)) 등에 부과되며, 대학원 진학 시 사전에 승인 절차를 밟아야 합니다.
conditions.waiver_en: Requires formal ministerial clearance before commencing postgraduate courses.

clause_notes_ko.text: 학생 주신청자뿐 아니라 동반가족(500.612(1)(d))에게도 부과되어 동반배우자가 호주에서 임의로 대학원에 진학하는 것을 통제합니다.

clause_notes_en.text: Applies both to specified primary and secondary student holders to vet postgraduate and bridging courses.

8204The holder must not undertake or change a course of study or research, or thesis or research topic, for:

unless approval is given by the Minister after the Minister has obtained an assessment from the competent Australian authorities that the holder is not likely to be directly or indirectly a risk to Australian national security.

conditions.title_ko: 학업·연수 전면 금지 (No Study)
conditions.title_en: No Study or Training in Australia
conditions.summary_ko: 기간의 장단에 관계없이(단 1일·1개월 단기 과정 포함) 호주에서 어떠한 학업이나 직업훈련도 받을 수 없습니다.
conditions.summary_en: You must not engage in any studies or training in Australia, regardless of duration.
forbidden_ko: 3개월 미만 단기 어학원이나 취미·직무 교육 과정을 포함한 일체의 학업·연수
forbidden_en: All forms of study or training in Australia, including short courses under 3 months
obligations_ko: 비자 기간 중 어떤 교육기관·훈련 프로그램에도 등록하지 않음
obligations_en: Do not enrol in or attend any study or training course
exceptions_ko: 8201(3개월 허용)과 달리 예외 조항이 없는 완전 금지 조항
exceptions_en: No short-study allowance (unlike 8201).
conditions.waiver_ko: 학업이 필요하면 8207이 없는 다른 비자를 발급받아야 합니다(주로 600 ADS 단체관광·050 BVE 등).
conditions.waiver_en: No built-in exception; study requires a visa without Condition 8207.

clause_notes_ko.text: 8201(3개월 이하 허용)과 혼동하기 쉬우나 8207은 '단 하루'의 학업·훈련도 금지합니다.

clause_notes_en.text: Absolute ban on study or training (stricter than 8201's 3-month limit).

conditions.statutory_text: 8207The holder must not engage in any studies or training in Australia.
statutory_paragraphs: 8207The holder must not engage in any studies or training in Australia.
conditions.dha_web_title: 8207 - No study
conditions.dha_web_summary:
You cannot undertake any studies or training in Australia.
